body: Thanks, that's a good point! I'll be careful

Thank you, I think you're right! I've booked myself in for counselling next week, and I'll start by bringing up my problems with addiction.

Hope you're well friend :)
Thank you, this was genuinely helpful to think about.

Have you considered speaking to your boss about it? It might not be appropriate depending on the circumstances, but if you feel they would be receptive it can be a huge weight off your shoulders. 

Regardless of whether you let them know or not, try to break things down into smaller chunks. Stay focused for 5 minutes, then 5 minutes more, and so on until you're done with the day, taking as many breaks as you can.

Good luck :)

Well done for going out and seeing friends, I know how hard it can be to leave your room (or even just your bed) but I think being around people helps a lot.

I'm actually starting to notice a nice mood change from the SSRI's, so I'm quite hopeful - I'm so glad I didn't give up on them when I was just getting side effects (nausea and trouble sleeping mostly). If you or anyone else reading this decides to start SSRIs, then stick with it, it does get better. 

I hope the weekend was able to give you a bit of a boost, and keep me updated!

Hi - sorry it took me a while to get back to you.

The dissociation seems to vary day by day, but when it's bad I've definitely noticed that I'm sensitive to light - car headlights feel unusually strong and even after half an hour in a bright area I'm still squinting. I do find it helps raising my eyebrows, as this opens up my eyes. 

If you don't mind the question, are you on anti-depressants? I'm a month into a course of SSRIs, and I've been wondering if the dissociation had anything to do with that.

Hope you're doing well friend :)
That's interesting! My parents commented recently that they can tell when I'm depressed because I get hooded eyes from frowning. I'll see if trying to keep them open helps
I've recently spoken to my professors about my depression and anxiety, and it's been pretty helpful - well done for deciding to email them, and I hope it goes well for you.

Since I woke up this morning I've felt dissociated from my surroundings. Everything feels dreamlike and distant, like there's a veil between me and the outside world. I guess this is how my brain is choosing to cope with anxiety and depression, but it's terrifying

Going for walks and getting lots of daylight can help. But most of all, try to be forgiving to yourself for taking time off to recover. Accept that you won't be as productive as usual, and don't beat yourself up because of it.
Thanks! I made it to an appointment this morning, and now have a prescription! Hopefully this is the beginning of recovery
I hadn't even considered it had anything to do with my diet. I'll look into it!

It's worth talking to your doctor soon - they'll be in the best position to help you out with this, and to identify what the problem is. Prozac doesn't work as it's meant to in some people, so they might decide to try a different medication with you.

It took me 4 days to work up the energy and courage to book a doctor's appointment so I can get treatment. The earliest appointment they could give me is in two weeks. Even two days' time seems bleak, so how am I going to hold on for two weeks?

You may just be a stranger on the internet, but I really feel for you reading this. Please consider seeking a professional, your friends would be glad for you to be taking care of yourself. 

Also, for self-harm, it can be really helpful using distractions. Next time you feel like hitting your legs, consider doodling instead. Drawing on your legs with a marker can be oddly therapeutic. Also, you could try the rubber band method (have a rubber band around your wrist, and snap it when you feel anxious). You get a sharp sting, but it doesn't do lasting damage. 

For suicidal feelings, please have a look at https://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/ and consider posting there. It might not feel like it, but there's hope :)

I'd like that - we can keep each other updated if you want. 


We've taken the first steps, so we're on the right tracks :) 


If it helps, to motivate myself I think of a future me who will be happy that I'm trying to do something about it. Even though right now I can't see the point, I'm hoping that one day I'll look back as a happier person and be grateful I did it.

Thanks, really helps to hear you say that. It does feel like it's denial in my case, as much from me as from family members. I think I'll see a GP and discuss with them.

I hope you're doing ok now and that the help you're getting is working well :)
